sentences.en: An extremely simplified way to explain J2's approach is that they're taking small bits of carbon and growing them into full diamonds.
sentences.zh: 用极其简化的方式来解释 J2 的方法，就是他们拿一小块碳，然后将其培育成长颗粒的完整钻石。

sentences.en: Almost in the same way you would grow a crop, where some turn out beautifully and some are duds.
sentences.zh: 这几乎就像种植农作物一样，有的长得精美绝伦，有的则长成了次品。

sentences.en: Like how some potatoes turn out hearty and strong, and others end up small or lopsided or heart-shaped.
sentences.zh: 就像有些土豆长得饱满结实，而另一些则又小又畸形，或者是心形的。

sentences.en: It's not a mass-produced thing.
sentences.zh: 这不是批量生产的产品。

sentences.en: It is an art.
sentences.zh: 这是一门艺术。

sentences.en: It is a complicated thing.
sentences.zh: 这是一件复杂的事情。

sentences.en: I'll probably put it a little more bluntly and say I think there's, as a scientist, of course, big caveat,
sentences.zh: 我可能会说得更直白一点，作为一名科学家，我当然要指出一个重大的前提,

sentences.en: there's tremendous beauty in being able to take essentially cow farts and converting it into this technologically advanced yet beautiful material.
sentences.zh: 那就是能够把基本上是牛屁的物质转化为这种科技感十足又美丽动人的材料，具有巨大的美学价值。

sentences.en: Diamonds have been synthesized in laboratories since 1950, but it used to be mostly for industrial uses,
sentences.zh: 自 1950 年代以来，实验室里就一直在合成钻石，但过去这主要用于工业用途，

sentences.en: like for surgical knives or the knives used to cut aluminum for iPhones.
sentences.zh: 比如手术刀，或者用于切割 iPhone 铝制外壳的刀具。

sentences.en: It's only very recently, like in the last couple of years, that laboratory-grown diamonds have started to look just as beautiful as the ones from the ground.
sentences.zh: 直到最近，也就是过去几年里，实验室培育的钻石才开始变得跟从地下挖出来的钻石一样美丽动人。

sentences.en: Again, John and Jonathan didn't set out to make engagement rings.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，约翰和乔纳森并不是一开始就打算制作订婚戒指的。

sentences.en: But businesses like theirs have put the traditional diamond industry on edge.
sentences.zh: 但像他们这样的企业让传统钻石行业感到如芒在背。

sentences.en: We've definitely seen significant growth in lab diamonds.
sentences.zh: 我们确实看到培育钻石取得了显著增长。

sentences.en: So consumer acceptance, particularly among millennial consumers, has increased.
sentences.zh: 因此，消费者的接受度，尤其是千禧一代消费者的接受度有所提高。

sentences.en: And you sell those here?
sentences.zh: 你们这里也卖这些吗？

sentences.en: We do.
sentences.zh: 我们卖的。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 噢，哇。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Catherine Money of Brilliant Earth told me that lab-grown diamonds are sold almost interchangeably with mined diamonds.
sentences.zh: “灿烂地球”（Brilliant Earth）的凯瑟琳·莫尼告诉我，培育钻石的销售几乎可以与开采的钻石互换。

sentences.en: They are also assessed for rarity using the four Cs.
sentences.zh: 人们同样会用“4C”标准来评估它们的稀有度。

sentences.en: The main difference is that they're cheaper.
sentences.zh: 主要的区别在于它们更便宜。

sentences.en: And generally, consumers are drawn to lab-graded diamonds because they're beautiful, they're responsible, and they're affordable.
sentences.zh: 一般来说，消费者会被实验室分级的钻石吸引，因为它们既美丽、负责任，又买得起。

sentences.en: Lab diamonds do use a lot of energy to keep the reactors humming.
sentences.zh: 培育钻石为了让反应炉持续运转确实消耗了大量能量。

sentences.en: But it's certainly less energy-intensive than digging a massive crater in the earth.
sentences.zh: 但与在地球上挖出一个巨大的弹坑相比，它消耗的能量肯定要少得多。

sentences.en: Lab diamonds seem like an ethical, attainable option,
sentences.zh: 培育钻石似乎是一个符合道德、触手可及的选择，

sentences.en: especially to a generation of marriage-aged consumers who are broke and were raised in the 90s and 2000s among whispers of blood diamonds.
sentences.zh: 特别是对一代正值适婚年龄的消费者来说，他们口袋空空，又是在 90 年代和 2000 年代伴随着血钻的窃窃私语中长大的。

sentences.en: The diamond industry is still reeling from that blood diamond reckoning over 20 years ago.
sentences.zh: 钻石行业至今仍未从 20 年前那场血钻算账的阴影中恢复过来。

sentences.en: Back then, De Beers was rightfully worried that people would boycott them and that the value of diamonds would plummet.
sentences.zh: 当时，戴比尔斯理所当然地担心人们会抵制它们，而且钻石的价值会暴跌。

sentences.en: So De Beers did something pretty drastic.
sentences.zh: 于是戴比尔斯采取了相当极端的做法。

sentences.en: They sold off a lot of their diamond reserve.
sentences.zh: 他们抛售了大量钻石储备。

sentences.en: They ended their own monopoly.
sentences.zh: 他们结束了自己的垄断地位。

sentences.en: Between, I would say, 2000 and 2004, De Beers liquidated their stockpile.
sentences.zh: 我想说，在 2000 年到 2004 年之间，戴比尔斯清空了他们的库存。

sentences.en: You saw other companies emerge in the space, other diamond producers.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到该领域涌现出其他公司、其他钻石生产商。

sentences.en: De Beers relinquished control of the global diamond supply.
sentences.zh: 戴比尔斯放弃了对全球钻石供应的控制权。

sentences.en: Consequently, they stopped advertising for all diamonds.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们停止了针对所有钻石的广告宣传。

sentences.en: De Beers went from being the only player in the industry to one of several.
sentences.zh: 戴比尔斯从行业中唯一的玩家变成了众多玩家之一。

sentences.en: And as a result, the mined diamond industry has slowed down a lot.
sentences.zh: 结果就是，开采钻石行业大大放缓了。

sentences.en: Almost nobody's exploring for diamonds.
sentences.zh: 几乎没有人再去勘探钻石了。

sentences.en: Nobody's building new diamond mines.
sentences.zh: 没有人再建造新的钻石矿了。

sentences.en: So I think we actually could run into a situation where there's like a shortage of diamonds in the future.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们实际上可能会陷入这样一种境地：未来可能会出现钻石短缺的情况。

sentences.en: Paul argues that in like five to ten years, diamonds from the earth will become rare again.
sentences.zh: 保罗认为，在五到十年内，来自地底的钻石将再次变得稀有。

sentences.en: Because fewer mines are being cultivated, that scarcity that De Beers faked through their monopoly might actually come true.
sentences.zh: 由于开采的矿山减少，戴比尔斯通过垄断伪造的那种稀缺性可能真的会变成现实。

sentences.en: So this means there's two kinds of diamonds in the market right now.
sentences.zh: 这意味着现在市场上存在两种钻石。

sentences.en: Mined or natural diamonds, the kind that are getting rarer and more expensive.
sentences.zh: 开采钻石或天然钻石，也就是变得越来越稀有、越来越昂贵的这种。

sentences.en: And lab-grown diamonds or man-made diamonds, which are proliferating and getting cheaper.
sentences.zh: 还有实验室培育钻石或人造钻石，它们产量激增且价格越来越便宜。

sentences.en: The question is, can you tell the difference?
sentences.zh: 问题是，你能看出区别吗？

sentences.en: And does it matter?
sentences.zh: 这重要吗？

sentences.en: So I think it's important to make the distinction that man-made and natural diamonds can be distinguished with certainty.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，明确指出人造钻石和天然钻石是可以确切区分开来的，这一点很重要。

sentences.en: They can.
sentences.zh: 它们确实可以区分。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, that's interesting that you're doing all this work and you didn't even realize that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，很有意思的是，你做了这么多工作，甚至都没有意识到这一点。

sentences.en: Listen, Paul.
sentences.zh: 听着，保罗。

sentences.en: I can't see the difference between lab diamonds and natural diamonds.
sentences.zh: 我看不出实验室钻石和天然钻石有什么区别。

sentences.en: You can't with the naked eye.
sentences.zh: 肉眼确实看不出来。

sentences.en: And even with the official fancy equipment, some diamond sellers in the diamond district can't tell the difference either.
sentences.zh: 而且即使有了官方的高级设备，钻石区的某些钻石商也分不清。

sentences.en: Very irregular teSt.
sentences.zh: 非常不规范的测试。

sentences.en: Diamond teSt.
sentences.zh: 钻石测试。

sentences.en: You say diamond book.
sentences.zh: 你说的是钻石书。

sentences.en: When I visited the diamond district, I asked a couple jewelers to look at a pair of lab-grown diamond earrings.
sentences.zh: 当我造访钻石区时，我请几位珠宝商看了一副实验室培育的钻石耳环。

sentences.en: I know for a fact that these earrings are lab-grown.
sentences.zh: 我很确凿地知道这些耳环是实验室培育的。

sentences.en: They were sent to me by a lab-grown diamond company.
sentences.zh: 是一家培育钻石公司寄给我的。

sentences.en: And these two diamond sellers, with booths across from each other, took turns testing each earring.
sentences.zh: 这两个在街对面拥有摊位的钻石商轮流测试了每一只耳环。

sentences.en: And I am fairly certain that they both got it wrong.
sentences.zh: 我相当确信他们两个都猜错了。

sentences.en: What did yours do?
sentences.zh: 你的测出来怎么样？

sentences.en: One-one.
sentences.zh: 一比一。

sentences.en: Yeah, mine was one-one.
sentences.zh: 对，我的是一比一。

sentences.en: That was actually a jackpot.
sentences.zh: 这其实算是个大奖。

sentences.en: He said, that one's a jackpot.
sentences.zh: 他说，那个是个大奖。

sentences.en: Because both jewelers told me that one earring was quote-unquote real, and the other was lab-grown.
sentences.zh: 因为两位珠宝商都告诉我，其中一只耳环是所谓的“真钻”，而另一只是培育钻石。

sentences.en: One diamond seller offered to buy the real diamond for between $500 to $1,000.
sentences.zh: 其中一位钻石商开价 500 到 1000 美元买下那颗真钻。
500 到 1000 美元可不是……

sentences.en: Nothing to sneeze at.
sentences.zh: 小钱。

sentences.en: It's not chicken feed, right.
sentences.zh: 不是什么微不足道的小数目，对吧。

sentences.en: And then the other one, you'd sell at a very low price.
sentences.zh: 然后另一颗，你得按很低的价格卖掉。

sentences.en: Like, what's a really low price for that one?
sentences.zh: 比如说，那颗的超低价是多少？

sentences.en: Like, $100?
sentences.zh: 比如 100 美元？

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: It's fake.
sentences.zh: 它是假的。

sentences.en: You know, it's not fake, but it's lab-grown.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它不是假的，但它是实验室培育的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I don't know if you could hear that, but he said the lab-grown diamond would only be worth about $100.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你能不能听到，但他说那颗培育钻石只值 100 美元左右。

sentences.en: So one earring was supposedly worth 10 times more than the other.
sentences.zh: 所以其中一只耳环的价值据称是另一只的 10 倍。

sentences.en: And again, I can't emphasize enough that this pair of earrings came from the same laboratory.
sentences.zh: 再次强调，我怎么强调都不为过，这副耳环来自同一个实验室。

sentences.en: We value diamonds for their perceived worth so much more than anything about the way they actually look.
sentences.zh: 我们对钻石的价值评估，比起它们实际的外观，更多地取决于我们心理上对它们价值的感知。

sentences.en: I sell an engagement ring for $2,000.
sentences.zh: 我以 2,000 美元的价格卖出一枚订婚戒指。

sentences.en: The guy goes, kid, you write an $8,000 appraisal.
sentences.zh: 那小伙子说，老弟，你给我开个 8,000 美元的估价单吧。

sentences.en: I can't do that.
sentences.zh: 我做不到。

sentences.en: I'm not doing that.
sentences.zh: 我不会那么做的。

sentences.en: You know, because they want to put that in front of the girl, you know, and say, I've ordered an $8,000 ring.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，因为他们想把那个摆在女孩面前，然后说，我定制了一枚 8,000 美元的戒指。

sentences.en: I mean, it's kind of smart, but...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这挺聪明的，但是……

sentences.en: Well, I always say, if you're going to start a relationship that way, it's not going very long.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我总是说，如果你打算以那种方式开始一段感情，它不会持续太久。

sentences.en: Never mind.
sentences.zh: 算了。

sentences.en: Not a good idea.
sentences.zh: 这不是个好主意。

sentences.en: Don't lie to your partner.
sentences.zh: 不要对你的伴侣撒谎。

sentences.en: But I guess it still just seems odd to talk about how much your proposal diamond costs if you can't see the difference.
sentences.zh: 但我想，如果你看不出区别，谈论你的求婚钻石花了多少钱，听起来还是挺奇怪的。

sentences.en: I mean, it shouldn't matter, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这不该重要，对吧？

sentences.en: And the question is, would proposing to someone with a $100 diamond, would that have kind of the same impact?
sentences.zh: 问题是，用一颗 100 美元的钻石向某人求婚，会产生同样的效果吗？

sentences.en: And this is, you know, something that's not practical or not rational.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这有点不切实际，也不够理性。

sentences.en: So I don't see a diamond as an investment in the material object, but it's probably an investment in a commitment that you're trying to portray.
sentences.zh: 所以我并不认为钻石是对物质本身的投资，它可能更多是对你想要展现的承诺的一种投资。

sentences.en: Catherine Money at Brilliant Earth gave me pretty much the same answer.
sentences.zh: “灿烂地球”的凯瑟琳·莫尼给我的答案几乎完全一样。

sentences.en: That diamonds are valuable because they are tied to our deepest relationships.
sentences.zh: 钻石之所以有价值，是因为它们与我们最深的情感联系在一起。

sentences.en: It's a representation of commitment and love and values.
sentences.zh: 它是承诺、爱和价值观的象征。

sentences.en: At the time, I thought this answer was a bit of an evasive cop-out, but it's not.
sentences.zh: 当时，我以为这个答案有点逃避现实的敷衍，但其实并不是。

sentences.en: This is how real, tangible value has been created and assigned.
sentences.zh: 这就是真实、有形价值被创造和赋予的方式。

sentences.en: By De Beers, sure, and by all of us.
sentences.zh: 当然是由戴比尔斯创造的，也是由我们所有人共同赋予的。

sentences.en: By everyone, myself included, who wondered if Courtney and Sean were really engaged without a ring.
sentences.zh: 由每个人，包括我自己——我也曾在心里琢磨过，考特尼和肖恩在没有戒指的情况下是否真的订婚了。

sentences.en: Without a diamond.
sentences.zh: 没有钻石。

sentences.en: I thought that I was better than that.
sentences.zh: 我以为我比那更高尚。

sentences.en: But you're not.
sentences.zh: 但你并没有。

sentences.en: But I'm not.
sentences.zh: 但我并没有。

sentences.en: Look at this friggin' sparkly thing.
sentences.zh: 看看这个该死闪闪发光的东西。

sentences.en: Let me see it.
sentences.zh: 让我看看。

sentences.en: It's so beautiful.
sentences.zh: 太美了。

sentences.en: Courtney caved.
sentences.zh: 考特尼妥协了。

sentences.en: I was like, okay, we can get rings.
sentences.zh: 我说，好吧，我们可以买戒指。

sentences.en: I give in.
sentences.zh: 我认输了。

sentences.en: But we have to get them vintage.
sentences.zh: 但我们必须买复古的。

sentences.en: If you really wanted to get a diamond and minimize your impact, a vintage diamond is the way to go.
sentences.zh: 如果你真的想买钻石并尽量减少对环境的影响，复古钻石是不二之选。

sentences.en: Compared to digging a massive hole in the earth or a room full of humming reactors, your grandmother's ring doesn't emit any fresh carbon.
sentences.zh: 与在地球上挖一个巨大的洞或坐落着满屋子轰鸣反应炉相比，你祖母的戒指不会排放任何新鲜碳。

sentences.en: We went to the Alameda flea market.
sentences.zh: 我们去了阿拉米达跳蚤市场。

sentences.en: Courtney's ring has not one, but two diamonds.
sentences.zh: 考特尼的戒指上不仅有一颗，而且有两颗钻石。

sentences.en: And in the center is a ruby.
sentences.zh: 正中心是一颗红宝石。

sentences.en: Sean's ring has a sapphire.
sentences.zh: 肖恩的戒指上有一颗蓝宝石。

sentences.en: It ended up being ruby and sapphire.
sentences.zh: 最后变成了红宝石和蓝宝石。

sentences.en: I ended up with ruby, which is the Pokemon game I'm playing.
sentences.zh: 我最后得到的是红宝石，正是我在玩的宝可梦游戏。

sentences.en: And Sean ended up with sapphire, which is the Pokemon game she's playing.
sentences.zh: 而肖恩得到的是蓝宝石，正是她正在玩的宝可梦游戏。

sentences.en: It's so cute.
sentences.zh: 太可爱了。

sentences.en: Their rings still fit into their nerdy little world.
sentences.zh: 他们的戒指依然契合他们书呆子般的小世界。

sentences.en: And even though diamond engagement rings are built on a bedrock of BS concocted tradition,
sentences.zh: 尽管钻石订婚戒指建立在胡扯和虚构传统的基石之上，

sentences.en: all traditions get made up somehow.
sentences.zh: 但所有的传统总归都是某种程度上捏造出来的。

sentences.en: And they become more authentic as they get ossified in time.
sentences.zh: 随着时间流逝逐渐根深蒂固，它们也就变得更加真实了。

sentences.en: Courtney and Sean love their rings.
sentences.zh: 考特尼和肖恩都很喜欢他们的戒指。

sentences.en: Yes, because they loved each other.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为他们深爱着彼此。

sentences.en: It is not, and has never been, a rational thing.
sentences.zh: 这从来不是一件理性的事情，现在也不是。

sentences.en: Pocket, a piece of paper, words from yesterday.
sentences.zh: 口袋，一张纸，昨日的话语。

sentences.en: There's a portrait painted on the things we love.
sentences.zh: 在我们所爱之物上绘有一幅肖像。

sentences.en: Articles of Interest was written and performed by Avery Truffleman.
sentences.zh: 《感兴趣的物品》（Articles of Interest）由艾弗里·特雷弗曼（Avery Truffleman）编剧并演播。

sentences.en: Insights, support, and edits from the whole 99PI team, including Vivian Leigh, Sean Rial, Abby Madon, Kurt Colstead, Delaney Hall, and Katie Mingle.
sentences.zh: 感谢整个 99PI 团队提供的见解、支持与编辑，包括薇薇安·莉（Vivian Leigh）、肖恩·里亚尔（Sean Rial）、艾比·马顿（Abby Madon）、库尔特·科尔斯特德（Kurt Colstead）、德兰妮·霍尔（Delaney Hall）和凯蒂·明格（Katie Mingle）。

sentences.en: And Roman Mars is the rare gem of this whole series.
sentences.zh: 而罗曼·马尔斯是整个系列中罕见的珍宝。

sentences.en: With the invention of the engagement ring came the invention of the engagement period.
sentences.zh: 随着订婚戒指的发明，订婚期也随之诞生。

sentences.en: A time where you have a ring on your finger, but you're not yet a spouse.
sentences.zh: 那是你手上戴着戒指，但还未成为配偶的一段时间。

sentences.en: It was an invention of a new stage of life.
sentences.zh: 这是对一种崭新人生阶段的发明。

sentences.en: The bride, the category of bride, when I use that word, I'm really using it in the way that the wedding industry uses it.
sentences.zh: 新娘，新娘这个范畴，当我使用这个词时，我其实是按照婚礼行业的使用方式来用的。

sentences.en: Which is to say this young woman who's at this stage of her life and that may be engaged and going through this process is an incredibly valuable proposition for all kinds of businesses.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，这位正处于人生这个阶段、可能已经订婚并正在经历这一过程的年轻女性，对各类企业来说都是一个极具价值的市场。

sentences.en: Author Rebecca Mead says someone used to be a bride for a day, and now you're a bride for as long as it takes to plan your wedding, which has gotten more and more elaborate.
sentences.zh: 作家丽贝卡·米德说，过去一个人只当一天新娘，而现在，只要筹备婚礼需要多久，你就会当多久的新娘，而且婚礼已经变得越来越繁复。

sentences.en: You know, I found an article that was published in 1939 called The Cost of Weddings in the American Sociological Review.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我找到了一篇1939年发表在《美国社会学评论》上、名为《婚礼成本》的文章。

sentences.en: And a third of the brides didn't have an engagement ring.
sentences.zh: 当时有三分之一的新娘没有订婚戒指。

sentences.en: 16% were married in clothes they already owned.
sentences.zh: 16%的新娘穿着自己原本就有的衣服结婚。

sentences.en: A third of them married without a wedding reception in addition to the ceremony.
sentences.zh: 其中三分之一的人结婚时除了仪式外没有举办婚宴。

sentences.en: And about a third of them didn't have a honeymoon.
sentences.zh: 大约三分之一的人没有度蜜月。

sentences.en: So these things that we think of as like absolutely core elements of what a wedding is just weren't necessarily core elements.
sentences.zh: 所以这些我们认为绝对是婚礼核心要素的东西，在当时并不一定是核心要素。

sentences.en: The wedding industry has emerged to convince brides that you're not really a bride without a massive cake, without a rehearsal dinner, without a lingerie set,
sentences.zh: 婚礼行业的兴起是为了让新娘相信，没有巨大的蛋糕、没有彩排晚宴、没有内衣套装，你就不算真正的新娘，

sentences.en: without something old and something new and something borrowed and something blue.
sentences.zh: 没有旧物、新物、借来的东西和蓝色的东西就不算完整。

sentences.en: And we all know that no one needs a party that might cost tens of thousands of dollars.
sentences.zh: 我们都知道，没有人非得办一场可能耗资数万美元的派对。

sentences.en: We live in a consumer culture.
sentences.zh: 我们生活在一个消费文化中。

sentences.en: We're not ignorant of the fact that we're being sold stuff that we don't need.
sentences.zh: 我们并非不知道自己正在被兜售不需要的东西。

sentences.en: And, you know, we all have some discretion and some sense of distance on that.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我们对此都有一定的自主权和距离感。

sentences.en: But when you're being told this is how it's done.
sentences.zh: 但当别人告诉你事情就该这么做时。

sentences.en: You just want to do it all the right way.
sentences.zh: 你只想把所有事情都做得恰到好处。

sentences.en: And if you don't do it like this, then, you know, maybe you're not doing it properly.
sentences.zh: 如果你不这样做，那么，你知道，也许你就没有做对。

sentences.en: And if you're not doing your wedding properly, maybe you're not properly committed to your marriage.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有把婚礼办好，也许说明你对婚姻的承诺不够坚定。

sentences.en: Your next articles of interest are wedding dresses.
sentences.zh: 你接下来感兴趣的文章是关于婚纱的。
